jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a hands-on, multi-disciplinary Chief Technology Officer to lead its end-to-end technology organization, spanning product engineering, IT infrastructure, and corporate and platform cybersecurity.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and partnering with executive leadership, this executive provides comprehensive oversight across technology, enterprise systems, and risk management. The Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer reports directly to this role.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Drive overall technology strategy, cloud infrastructure, and technical execution for the organization's core SaaS platform.
Manage the enterprise technology budget and drive cost optimization across software licensing, infrastructure procurement, hardware lifecycles, and vendor contracts.
Partner with executive leadership to transition new products from beta to market launch while actively managing technical debt.
Advise the CEO and Board of Directors on enterprise technical risk, disaster recovery, business continuity planning, and corporate cyber resilience.
Oversee day-to-day corporate IT operations, including endpoint management, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, and multi-tier helpdesk support.
Administer enterprise productivity suites and communication architectures while enforcing zero-trust access controls, single sign-on (SSO), and document retention policies.
Oversee business system infrastructure in close alignment with organizational leadership to ensure high uptime and integration security.
Direct organization-wide information security initiatives across corporate endpoints, networks, and SaaS tools.
Establish and audit enterprise IT policies, including acceptable use, zero-trust identity and access management (IAM), data loss prevention (DLP), and offboarding protocols.
Enforce compliance and audit readiness—including SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, ISO 27001, and c3/c4 non-profit legal boundaries—in collaboration with Legal, HR, and Finance.
Evaluate alpha projects and proofs of concept across departments, guiding execution to integrate them into the core SaaS platform or architect them as standalone, scalable services.
Mitigate vendor lock-in risk by establishing standardized data portability and integration frameworks across corporate SaaS applications.
Serve as direct manager to the Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer (CPEDO), establishing shared goals and aligning product, engineering, and data strategies with enterprise infrastructure and security standards.
Partner with the CPEDO on budget, resourcing, and prioritization trade-offs across product, engineering, and data initiatives.
Build, mentor, and scale a service-oriented IT and security team aligned with organizational growth objectives.
Establish pragmatic automated internal processes that maintain rigorous security standards without introducing operational friction for staff.

Qualifications

12+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including roles such as Director of IT, Head of IT/Operations Technology, VP of IT, or Chief Technology Officer.
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise IT and information security stacks, zero-trust architectures, IAM, and automated endpoint management.
Experience driving capital and operational expenditure (CapEx/OpEx) strategies for corporate IT, including SaaS license management, hardware procurement cycles, and third-party vendor governance.
Proven track record leading enterprise security operations and successfully navigating SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 audit cycles.
Expertise in architecting, securing, and administering enterprise collaboration platforms and workplace productivity suites.
Proven track record of building and leading technical teams across a broad range of expertise.
Experience building or scaling an internal IT function through periods of organizational growth.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical staff, executive leadership, and Board members.

Compensation and Benefits

Annual salary: $220,000 to $230,000,
commensurate with experience.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options.
403(b) retirement plan with an employer match.
Paid vacation, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Paid parental leave.
Professional development and education reimbursement assistance.
Monthly technology and wellness stipend.

Additional Information

Essential duties reflect the primary functions assigned to this role and may be adjusted or reassigned at any time.
Employees must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations will be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions, absent undue hardship.
The organization maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding abuse and inappropriate behavior.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate IT
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking an AI-forward Director, Corporate IT to lead the corporate technology function. This is a full-time role located in the United States.

This leader will oversee IT operations, employee technology, enterprise business applications, integrations, workflow automation, and AI enablement for internal productivity and corporate operations. The role leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for delivering secure, reliable, and intuitive technology experiences across the organization.

The enterprise business applications portfolio includes internal systems supporting People, Finance, Accounting, Legal, Procurement, and Operations. This position requires a leader experienced in modernizing an IT or enterprise technology function through automation, intelligent self-service, AI agents, and integrated business systems, rather than focusing primarily on traditional infrastructure, administration, and ticket resolution.

Responsibilities

Define and execute the strategy and roadmap for corporate IT, integrations, automation, and AI, while establishing enterprise standards for business applications.
Deliver a secure, reliable, and frictionless employee technology experience while evolving IT operations from reactive support toward proactive, automated service delivery.
Partner with organizational leadership to enhance business processes, eliminate manual workflows, and identify high-value automation and AI opportunities.
Lead the evaluation, implementation, governance, and adoption of AI-enabled tools, agents, self-service capabilities, and workflow automation.
Ensure AI and automation solutions incorporate appropriate security, privacy, data access, human oversight, monitoring, and accountability.
Oversee core IT platforms and services, including identity and access management, Google Workspace, endpoint management, networking, collaboration tools, IT service management, and employee lifecycle processes.
Partner with business owners to govern enterprise applications—including HR, finance, accounting, procurement, and related internal systems—ensuring proper integration, security, reliability, lifecycle management, and vendor oversight.
Partner with Security to deploy and operate security technologies, enforce access controls, conduct periodic access reviews, support audits, and maintain secure onboarding and offboarding practices.
Manage the IT and enterprise applications budget, vendors, licensing, service levels, and performance metrics in alignment with broader technology strategy.

Qualifications

8+ years of progressive experience in corporate IT and enterprise technology, including at least 5 years leading teams and cross-functional technology programs.
Experience overseeing core IT platforms and services, including identity and access management, endpoint management, collaboration platforms, networking, IT service management, and employee lifecycle processes.
A proven record of deploying AI agents, copilots, intelligent automation, self-service capabilities, or AI-enabled support into governed production environments, achieving meaningful adoption and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success using low-code, no-code, integration, or workflow technologies to automate processes across multiple systems and business functions.
Experience partnering with business owners to govern internal enterprise applications such as HRIS, ERP, finance and accounting systems, procurement platforms, and business workflow tools.
Experience leading enterprise application implementations, migrations, integrations, or optimization programs.
Strong understanding of APIs, workflow orchestration, data flows, access controls, and application lifecycle management.
Experience partnering with Security to deploy and operate security technologies, manage access controls, conduct access reviews, support audits, and maintain secure onboarding and offboarding processes.
Experience managing IT and enterprise application budgets, vendors, contracts, licensing, service levels, and delivery partners.
Strong business judgment with the ability to communicate technology strategy, value, risks, and tradeoffs to executive leadership.
Demonstrated success leading organizational change and driving adoption of new tools and operating practices.

Benefits

Health and wellness coverage
Retirement benefits
Paid time off and paid holidays
Paid parental leave
Education assistance and professional development

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Director of Information Technology
will oversee the internal technology estate end to end and lead the team responsible for running it. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, this full-time role based in the United States covers identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, service management, and the internal artificial intelligence platform across a distributed, remote-first organization.

This position is designed for a leader experienced in building and scaling internal technology through periods of rapid growth, possessing the capability to construct a multi-year roadmap while maintaining the ability to resolve operational issues directly. The role collaborates closely with Security, Engineering, Finance, and Human Resources leadership while managing vendor and managed service provider relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Build and execute a multi-year internal technology roadmap across identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, and service management.
Tie technology investments directly to business outcomes with defined success measures.
Define internal delivery models versus services managed through partners and managed service providers.
Establish IT governance, operating standards, architecture reviews, and change management.
Design the internal IT function, build business cases for headcount, and hire and develop team members.
Mentor the team and establish clear ownership, on-call schedules, and escalation models.
Build and maintain the internal service catalog and associated service level agreements.
Own internal AI tool use case development, rollout, training, and adoption measurement.
Partner with the organization's AI practice so internal usage directly informs client-facing delivery.
Apply financial engineering to the internal AI estate by developing unit-cost models, forecasting consumption, negotiating commitments and reserved capacity, and holding AI expenditures accountable to measured productivity gains.
Own endpoint management, configuration baselines, patching, and hardware lifecycles using Intune or equivalent systems.
Manage the Microsoft 365 collaboration environment, including Teams, SharePoint, and Exchange governance.
Define and enforce device posture requirements for a remote-first workforce.
Direct internal network architecture, remote access, and secure connectivity models.
Manage the internal cloud and hosting footprint, including capacity, cost, and resilience.
Direct backup, recovery, and business continuity for internal systems with tested recovery objectives.
Establish and mature IT service management across intake, incident, problem, request, and change processes.
Publish operational metrics and systematically eliminate key sources of employee workflow friction.
Oversee the onboarding and offboarding technology experience in partnership with Human Resources.
Manage the internal IT budget, financial forecasts, and software licensing positions.
Rationalize the SaaS estate and direct renewals, contract negotiations, and vendor terms.
Hold external partners and managed service providers accountable to defined service levels.
Partner with security leadership to execute the IT components of the broader security program.
Support SOC 2 and ISO audit readiness, including control operation and evidence collection.
Own vulnerability management and remediation across internal systems and endpoints.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of information technology experience, including proven experience leading teams or owning a technology function.
Demonstrated experience building and scaling internal IT within a distributed or remote-first company during periods of rapid growth.
Experience presenting technology strategy, investment recommendations, operational risks, and performance metrics to executive leadership.
Deep hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint management (Intune or equivalent), and SaaS administration at scale.
Demonstrated ownership of internal AI adoption and governance, including policy creation, data handling, and change management.
Strong security fluency, with the ability to partner credibly with executive security leadership and translate technical risk into business terms.
Proven experience supporting SOC 2, ISO, or related regulated compliance and audit requirements.
Experience managing IT budgets and negotiating contracts with vendors and managed service providers.
Ability to communicate technical trade-offs clearly to both executive and technical audiences, in writing and in person.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience operating within a solutions provider, managed service provider (MSP), or technology consulting environment.
Relevant industry certifications, such as ITIL, Microsoft certifications, CISSP, CISM, PMP, or equivalent credentials.

Compensation and Benefits

Full-time employment status.
Discretionary incentive compensation and bonus opportunities based on individual and organizational performance.
Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with an employer match.
Flexible time off, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Short-term and long-term disability insurance.
Life insurance.
Paid parental leave.

Employment Notices

The organization is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. Qualified candidates are considered without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, final compensation is determined based on experience, skills, and location. The organization participates in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility and provides reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process upon request.

jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a Director, IT & Business Enablement
to oversee the systems, tools, and technology experience that support every internal team. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring that internal tools are fast, reliable, and user-friendly, while maximizing leverage from artificial intelligence across organizational systems.

This position oversees the complete lifecycle of the internal technology stack, encompassing endpoint provisioning, SaaS tooling, and the strategic adoption, integration, and optimization of AI. You will serve as the primary leader for organizational equipment and tooling needs, collaborate closely with finance on software utilization and budgeting, and automate processes to build scalable internal systems.

Key Responsibilities

Own, build, and scale the team and systems supporting internal IT infrastructure.
Manage company technology needs end-to-end, including new hire equipment, IT onboarding, and day-to-day productivity tools.
Hire, mentor, and develop members of the IT team to support the evolving needs of a global workforce.
Own the complete endpoint lifecycle, including provisioning, application deployment, endpoint patching, and asset retirement.
Manage and administer identity systems enabling secure access to corporate infrastructure and applications.
Enable secure AI adoption across the organization by identifying workflow improvements, leading the integration of AI capabilities, and optimizing tooling for performance and ROI.
Evaluate, select, and manage the internal software and tooling stack to ensure appropriate utilization and effectiveness.
Lead hardware and software budget planning and vendor management in partnership with finance.
Develop and maintain comprehensive documentation for IT processes, systems, and support workflows.
Create and deliver internal training programs on systems and tools to drive company-wide adoption.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in IT management, systems administration, or technology operations.
5+ years of experience directly leading and managing a team.
Proven experience owning endpoint lifecycle management at scale, including provisioning, deployment, and retirement.
Hands-on experience administering a modern SaaS tooling stack, including identity and access management, mobile device management (MDM), and collaboration tools, with experience making build-versus-buy and consolidate-versus-expand decisions.
Demonstrated experience integrating AI tools into business workflows and leading adoption across a team or company, such as deploying AI-powered support tools, automating workflows, or evaluating AI vendor solutions.
Experience managing hardware and software budgets and vendor relationships, including translating technical decisions into financial and ROI terms for leadership.

jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The hiring organization is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
to lead the technology capabilities that keep digital products, cloud platforms, and internal teams secure, reliable, and productive.

This role oversees cloud infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, bot mitigation, corporate IT, and helpdesk support, while providing architectural leadership across cloud platforms, networking, identity, observability, and operational tooling. This position spans both internal employee technology and the production infrastructure supporting high-traffic, customer-facing applications.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead teams responsible for cloud infrastructure, SRE, production operations, corporate IT, helpdesk, and bot mitigation, establishing ownership, operational standards, service-level objectives (SLOs), escalation procedures, and performance metrics.
Develop managers, technical leads, and IT staff through coaching, career development, and building a culture of accountability, documentation, automation, and continuous improvement.
Build quarterly and annual infrastructure roadmaps aligned with business priorities, growth, security, reliability, and cost, partnering with engineering, product, data, marketing, finance, HR, legal, and executive leadership.
Own the reliability, scalability, security, performance, and cost-effectiveness of cloud infrastructure, primarily within AWS.
Provide architectural leadership across cloud services, applications, APIs, networking, identity, databases, storage, observability, and integrations while establishing architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and technical review processes.
Partner with engineering to improve deployment safety, performance, and readiness, driving automation, configuration management, and infrastructure as code.
Lead capacity planning for growth and demand spikes, eliminating single points of failure, undocumented systems, manual processes, and single-source dependencies.
Ensure production and nonproduction environments are properly separated, secured, and monitored, reviewing new systems for architectural fit, supportability, security, and total cost of ownership.
Establish and maintain service-level indicators (SLIs), SLOs, availability targets, and error-budget practices for critical systems.
Improve observability through centralized logging, metrics, distributed tracing, application performance monitoring (APM), and actionable alerting.
Lead major incident management, coordination, executive communication, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action tracking to improve mean time to detect, respond, and recover.
Develop and test backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures, and establish sustainable on-call practices.
Own strategy and tooling for bot mitigation, scraping protection, automated abuse prevention, and traffic-quality management using technologies such as Cloudflare, DataDome, web application firewalls (WAFs), rate limiting, CAPTCHA alternatives, and device fingerprinting.
Partner with cross-functional teams to distinguish malicious automation from legitimate customers, search engines, partners, and approved AI crawlers, establishing monitoring and response procedures.
Oversee internal IT services and helpdesk support, establishing service-level expectations for response times, resolution times, user satisfaction, and backlog reduction.
Manage the employee technology lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning, access management, asset recovery, and device inventory.
Standardize endpoint configuration, encryption, patching, and endpoint detection across laptops, collaboration platforms, productivity software, and telecom services.
Establish consistent identity and access management practices across corporate and production systems, implementing role-based access, least privilege, multi-factor authentication (MFA), periodic access reviews, and secure administrative account handling.
Support vulnerability remediation, security assessments, audits, vendor reviews, incident readiness, and applicable privacy requirements in partnership with legal and security teams.
Manage infrastructure, security, IT, telecom, monitoring, and support vendors, handling evaluations, contract reviews, renewals, licensing, service level agreements (SLAs), and budget management.
Improve cloud cost visibility through tagging, allocation, forecasting, tool consolidation, and contract optimization.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, SRE, platform engineering, DevOps, IT operations, or related disciplines.
5+ years of experience leading engineering or technology teams, including managing managers or technical leads.
Demonstrated experience operating high-traffic, customer-facing platforms in AWS or a comparable cloud environment.
Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, identity, security, observability, databases, APIs, storage, and distributed systems.
Experience managing production availability, incident response, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Experience with infrastructure automation, configuration management, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Experience managing corporate IT, employee support, endpoint management, software licensing, and access provisioning.
Experience establishing operational metrics, SLOs, and support standards.
Demonstrated ability to manage vendors, contracts, departmental budgets, and cloud costs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical risks, architecture, and tradeoffs to executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Cloudflare, DataDome, or comparable bot-management and web application protection platforms, including leading bot mitigation or traffic-quality programs.
Experience with AWS services, containerized environments, infrastructure as code, centralized logging, and APM tools (such as AppDynamics).
Experience supporting large-scale consumer subscription, public-record, data-as-a-service, advertising, or ecommerce platforms.
Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure, transitioning systems from external vendors, and consolidating cloud accounts or IT services.
Familiarity with privacy requirements and secure handling of sensitive consumer data.
Experience building or maturing SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering functions.

Measures of Success

Improved availability, performance, and stability of customer-facing platforms.
Reduced impact and infrastructure costs associated with bots, scraping, and automated abuse.
Faster incident detection, response, and recovery, alongside a reduction in recurring incidents.
Enhanced observability with reduced alert noise, validated disaster recovery capabilities, and optimized cloud spend.
Consistent helpdesk performance, reliable onboarding and offboarding, and robust endpoint security and asset tracking.
Strong architecture governance, reduced dependency on undocumented systems or vendors, and demonstrated team development.

Compensation and Benefits

Annual base salary: $170,000 - $180,000

Comprehensive health coverage including medical, dental, and vision insurance
Life insurance
Retirement benefits with employer match

jobs.description:
Job Posting Title:

Chief Information Officer, Texas McCombs

Hiring Department:

Red McCombs School of Business

Position Open To:

All Applicants

Weekly Scheduled Hours:

40

FLSA Status:

Exempt from FLSA

Earliest Start Date:

Immediately

Position Duration:

Expected to Continue Until Aug 31, 2027

Location:

UT MAIN CAMPUS

Job Details:

General Notes

Texas McCombs is a top business school at the center of one of the most innovative cities in the U.S. The McCombs community champions hands-on experiences alongside the ground-breaking research and thought-leadership of a world-class faculty. The collaborative spirit and enterprising drive of the Longhorn alumni network, one of the largest university networks in the world, is embedded in our culture, making us human-centered and future-focused in all our endeavors. We are shaping those who will shape tomorrow, and solving challenging problems while remaining committed to creating a community that is dynamic, supportive, and challenging. What starts here really does change the world.

For more information about Texas McCombs please visit: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/

Purpose

The Chief Information Officer is the senior information technology executive for the McCombs School of Business. Reporting to the Senior Associate Dean for Business Affairs and Chief Operating Officer, the CIO leads McCombs Technology Solutions (MTS), sets the school’s technology strategy, priorities, and investments, and advises the Dean and senior leaders on technology opportunities, risk, modernization, data, and artificial intelligence. The CIO provides executive leadership for technology operations, application development and data services, classroom and audiovisual technology, technology governance and project portfolio management, information security coordination, and technology contracting. The CIO represents McCombs within UT Austin’s federated technology environment and works closely with Enterprise Technology, the Information Security Office, the Office of Academic Technology, and the McCombs Office of Instructional Innovation.

Responsibilities

Technology Strategy, Governance, and Executive Advisory. Establish and execute McCombs’ technology strategy in alignment with school and university goals. Advise the Dean, COO, and senior leaders on technology investments, risks, opportunities, and trends. Lead the McCombs Technology Governance Process and oversee the technology project portfolio, prioritizing initiatives by institutional value, cost, risk, and sustainability. Represent McCombs in university technology planning and governance.
Technology Operations and Academic Technology Support. Provide executive oversight for technology operations, end-user support, device lifecycle management, school-managed infrastructure, and classroom and audiovisual technology. Support faculty technical needs for teaching and research, including specialized software, cloud environments, datasets, and AI platforms. Partner with the Office of Instructional Innovation, which leads pedagogy and instructional design, while MTS provides the supporting technical platforms and support.
Applications, Data, Modernization, AI, and Innovation. Oversee application development, databases, reporting, analytics, and integrations. Set priorities for modernizing legacy systems, reducing technical debt, and addressing single points of failure. Partner with data owners to improve data governance, quality, and access. Lead McCombs’ adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, with practices that address security, privacy, compliance, cost, and long-term support.
Information Security, Risk, and Resilience. Partner with the UT Austin Information Security Office to protect McCombs systems and data. Oversee vulnerability remediation, risk assessment, compliance, incident coordination, and security awareness. Communicate material technology risks and recommended actions to senior leadership, and strengthen business continuity for critical systems.
Organizational, Financial, and Vendor Leadership. Lead MTS, including Applications and Data, Technology Operations, Audio/Visual Technology, and Technology Planning and Strategy. Set performance expectations and service standards; recruit, develop, and retain staff and build depth through cross-training and succession planning. Oversee technology budgets, licensing, contracts, procurement, and vendor relationships in partnership with McCombs Financial Affairs, UT Procurement, and Legal Affairs.
Other duties as assigned in support of the mission and priorities of the McCombs School of Business.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and at least 10 years of progressively responsible information technology leadership experience, including significant responsibility for technology strategy, staff, budgets, vendors, and major technology initiatives.
Demonstrated experience leading a broad technology organization or portfolio spanning several areas such as application development, data and analytics, infrastructure, end-user services, cybersecurity, cloud services, or technology planning.
Experience developing and executing technology strategy and leading significant modernization, digital transformation, systems implementation, or organizational change initiatives.
Demonstrated experience managing technology professionals and leaders, including staff development, performance management, and organizational planning.
Experience with technology budgeting, vendor management, contracting, procurement, and major technology investments.
Knowledge of cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity, data management, and IT governance.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior executives, communicate complex technology issues to nontechnical audiences, and make sound recommendations involving cost, risk, and priorities.
Demonstrated success working with varied stakeholders and leading through influence in a complex organization.
Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate

Preferred Qualifications

Experience serving as a CIO, CTO, senior technology executive, or in a comparable enterprise technology leadership role.
Experience leading technology in higher education, government, another public institution, or a similarly complex, mission-driven organization, particularly within Texas.
Experience working within a federated or decentralized technology environment.
Experience with application development, system integration, data and analytics, enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, cybersecurity, and project portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience modernizing legacy applications or reducing significant technical debt.
Experience establishing or leading technology governance and enterprise project prioritization processes.
Experience developing organizational approaches to artificial intelligence or other emerging technologies.
Experience supporting technology requirements for academic instruction or research.
Experience with University of Texas policies, procedures, and administrative systems.

Salary Range

OPEN

Working Conditions

Works in standard office conditions.
Some evening and weekend hours may be required for system incidents, critical deadlines, and school or industry events.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Digital & Technology System Ownership
jobs.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

BeOne is a global biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery and development of innovative drug therapies for the treatment of cancer. At BeOne we believe that access to life-changing medicine sees no borders.

The Senior Manager, Global Digital & Technology System Ownership is accountable for the day-to-day ownership, operational health, lifecycle execution, and compliant management of Global Patient Safety R&D externally developed platforms and validated systems within the global R&D technology portfolio.

This role translates the GRDTS system ownership model into disciplined execution across technical configuration, platform operations, lifecycle planning, release and upgrade coordination, access management, documentation, security activities, vendor delivery, budget inputs, and inspection-ready evidence.

The Senior Manager partners with R&D business process owners, Global Technology Solutions, Information Security, Quality, vendors, Finance, Procurement, project teams, and support functions to ensure assigned platforms remain compliant, secure, reliable, supportable, and aligned with scientific and business needs.

The successful candidate brings strong regulated-systems experience specifically in Safety systems, hands-on operational leadership, structured problem solving, and the ability to coordinate global stakeholders through platform changes, incidents, competing priorities, and complex technical dependencies.

Essential Functions Of The Job

System Ownership Execution & Governance

Execute the system ownership model for Global Patient Safety’s externally developed platforms, maintaining clear accountability for business purposes, technical health, compliance posture, roadmap, support model, and lifecycle status.
Maintain system governance routines, decision logs, ownership records, operating controls, documentation standards, and cross-functional action tracking for validated and non-validated platforms.
Serve as the primary operational escalation point for assigned platforms, coordinating issue prioritization, risk review, lifecycle recommendations, and stakeholder alignment.

Technical Configuration, Platform Implementation, Upgrades & Integrations

Lead and coordinate technical configuration, platform implementation, upgrade readiness, integration changes, environment preparation, testing support, release execution, and post-release stabilization for assigned platforms for Global Patient Safety such as Argus, Case Intake system, Signal Detection platform, and Safety data mart and etc.
Ensure implementation and change plans align with Enterprise IT standards, cybersecurity requirements, validation expectations, business readiness, data and integration needs, and operational support models.
Manage dependencies, risks, communications, cutover activities, vendor deliverables, and stabilization actions for upgrades, integrations, enhancements, and platform modernization efforts.

System Life-Cycle Management & Roadmap Execution

Manage lifecycle activities for assigned systems, including onboarding, capability expansion, roadmap maintenance, technical debt reduction, modernization, retirement, and transition planning.
Convert business needs, platform needs, functions, features, technical constraints, and compliance requirements into executable roadmap items and prioritized delivery plans.
Coordinate feature and functionality additions, edits, and enhancements with business owners, technical teams, Enterprise IT, vendors, and Quality stakeholders.

Operational Excellence for Validated Systems

Own execution and monitoring of validated-system operations, including user access workflows, role governance, audit trail review, periodic review, security checks, evidence collection, and remediation tracking.
Ensure operating activities are consistently performed, documented, inspection-ready, and aligned with GxP, computer systems validation, 21 CFR Part 11, internal SOPs, and Quality expectations.
Identify and implement improvements to operational controls, review cadence, exception management, metrics, and issue closure practices.

System Documentation & SOP Management

Create, maintain, and periodically refresh system ownership artifacts, configuration records, technical operating procedures, administration and user access SOPs, support playbooks, and other system documentation.
Ensure documentation reflects current configuration, access models, integrations, lifecycle status, change history, operating procedures, support arrangements, and inspection-readiness needs.
Coordinate SOP creation, review, approval, training impacts, evidence readiness, and audit response activities with Quality, business process owners, and system teams.

System Security, Patch, Certificate & SSO Coordination

Coordinate system security and maintenance activities, including patch planning, vulnerability remediation, certificate renewals, single sign-on coordination, identity and access dependencies, and risk-based prioritization.
Partner with Enterprise IT and Information Security to plan and execute security actions in alignment with corporate policies, system criticality, business continuity needs, validation requirements, and change controls.
Maintain visibility of security risks, exceptions, remediation owners, due dates, evidence, and closure status through appropriate governance and escalation channels.

Budget Support, AOP & Vendor Management

Develop annual operating plan inputs for assigned platforms, including license, maintenance, upgrade, support, vendor, implementation, and lifecycle investment assumptions.
Manage vendor operational performance, service reviews, roadmap follow-up, escalations, contract and statement-of-work inputs, renewal preparation, deliverables, and action closure.
Partner with Finance, Procurement, Legal, business owners, and vendors to track spend, commitments, renewals, service expectations, and delivery against agreed business priorities.

Incident, Issue & Platform Problem Management

Lead operational response for platform incidents, recurring problems, integration failures, access issues, service disruptions, security events, and vendor delivery issues within assigned scope.
Coordinate root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, communications, service restoration, risk documentation, escalation, and status reporting.
Convert recurring platform issues into sustainable remediation plans, roadmap items, support model improvements, operating control changes, or vendor actions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Team Leadership

Represent assigned system ownership priorities in working sessions and governance forums with R&D functions, Enterprise IT, Information Security, Quality, Finance, Procurement, and vendors.
Lead and coach system owners, system managers, administrators, contractors, and matrixed partners in disciplined system ownership, compliant execution, technical rigor, and reliable service delivery.
Contribute to GRDTS portfolio transparency, prioritization, audit and inspection readiness, operational metrics, and continuous improvement of technology operating practices.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Collaborate with System Owners, System Managers, or other assigned GRDTS resources responsible for platform operations, lifecycle activities, documentation, and validated-system execution.
Coordinate matrixed technical resources, vendor partners, contractors, system administrators, and project teams supporting assigned systems and platform initiatives.

Key Capabilities

System ownership execution: applying accountable ownership models, governance routines, lifecycle controls, operating standards, and escalation pathways for R&D platforms and validated systems.
Platform delivery and operations: coordinating configuration, implementation, integrations, upgrades, releases, roadmap items, technical debt actions, and operational stabilization.
Regulated systems management: executing user access workflows, audit trail review, periodic review, SOP alignment, evidence management, remediation tracking, and inspection readiness.
Security and resilience coordination: managing patch, certificate, SSO, vulnerability, incident, continuity, and risk activities with Enterprise IT, Information Security, Quality, and vendors.
Vendor and financial stewardship: preparing budget inputs, monitoring spend, managing service performance, supporting renewals, and tracking vendor commitments to closure.

Key Competencies

Systems thinking across business processes, platform configuration, integrations, data flows, access controls, compliance requirements, and operational support models.
Cross-functional influence and clear communication with R&D, Enterprise IT, Information Security, Quality, Finance, Procurement, Legal, vendors, and global stakeholders.
Operational rigor, inspection-ready execution, sound judgment, structured problem solving, and the ability to convert ambiguous issues into clear actions and decisions.
Composed incident leadership during outages, upgrades, integration disruptions, security issues, and vendor escalations.
People leadership, coaching, prioritization, delegation, and accountability across direct, matrixed, contractor, and vendor resources.

Key Deliverables

Assigned-system ownership package covering accountability, governance cadence, lifecycle status, operating controls, documentation, metrics, risks, decisions, and escalations.
System roadmap and execution plan covering business needs, functions, features, integrations, dependencies, lifecycle milestones, enhancement priorities, technical debt, and risk actions.
Validated-system operations package covering access workflows, audit trail review, periodic review, evidence standards, SOP alignment, remediation tracking, and inspection readiness.
System security and maintenance tracker covering patches, certificate renewals, SSO coordination, vulnerability remediation, security exceptions, owners, due dates, evidence, and closure.
Budget and vendor management materials covering annual operating plan inputs, renewals, service reviews, vendor commitments, contract and statement-of-work inputs, escalation logs, and performance follow-up.
Incident and problem management records, including root-cause summaries, corrective and preventive action plans, stakeholder updates, decision logs, and durable remediation actions.

Other Qualifications

7+ years of professional experience in digital, technology, information systems, R&D technology, application operations, systems engineering, or related areas; pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or regulated healthcare experience strongly preferred.
4+ years of progressive leadership or management experience coordinating technical teams, matrixed partners, vendor resources, and cross-functional delivery across global or complex operating environments.
Demonstrated experience owning or managing business-critical platforms, including configuration, implementation, integrations, release and upgrade planning, access workflows, documentation, operational controls, incident management, and production support.
Strong working knowledge and hands on experience in managing safety case processing platform, case intake system, signal detection system, safety data marts and reports.
Strong working knowledge of GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, computer systems validation, change control, audit trail review, periodic review, SOP governance, inspection readiness, and regulated system operations.
Demonstrated ability to partner with Enterprise IT, Information Security, Quality, Finance, Procurement, Legal, vendors, business process owners, and global R&D

Texas McCombs is a top business school at the center of one of the most innovative cities in the U.S. The McCombs community champions hands-on experiences alongside the ground-breaking research and thought-leadership of a world-class faculty. The collaborative spirit and enterprising drive of the Longhorn alumni network, one of the largest university networks in the world, is embedded in our culture, making us human-centered and future-focused in all our endeavors. We are shaping those who will shape tomorrow, and solving challenging problems while remaining committed to creating a community that is dynamic, supportive, and challenging. What starts here really does change the world.

For more information about Texas McCombs please visit: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/

Purpose

The Chief Information Officer is the senior information technology executive for the McCombs School of Business. Reporting to the Senior Associate Dean for Business Affairs and Chief Operating Officer, the CIO leads McCombs Technology Solutions (MTS), sets the school’s technology strategy, priorities, and investments, and advises the Dean and senior leaders on technology opportunities, risk, modernization, data, and artificial intelligence. The CIO provides executive leadership for technology operations, application development and data services, classroom and audiovisual technology, technology governance and project portfolio management, information security coordination, and technology contracting. The CIO represents McCombs within UT Austin’s federated technology environment and works closely with Enterprise Technology, the Information Security Office, the Office of Academic Technology, and the McCombs Office of Instructional Innovation.

Responsibilities

Technology Strategy, Governance, and Executive Advisory. Establish and execute McCombs’ technology strategy in alignment with school and university goals. Advise the Dean, COO, and senior leaders on technology investments, risks, opportunities, and trends. Lead the McCombs Technology Governance Process and oversee the technology project portfolio, prioritizing initiatives by institutional value, cost, risk, and sustainability. Represent McCombs in university technology planning and governance.
Technology Operations and Academic Technology Support. Support faculty technical needs for teaching and research, including specialized software, cloud environments, datasets, and AI platforms. Partner with the Office of Instructional Innovation, which leads pedagogy and instructional design, while MTS provides the supporting technical platforms and support.

Lead McCombs’ adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, with practices that address security, privacy, compliance, cost, and long-term support.
Information Security, Risk, and Resilience. Partner with the UT Austin Information Security Office to protect McCombs systems and data. Oversee vulnerability remediation, risk assessment, compliance, incident coordination, and security awareness. Communicate material technology risks and recommended actions to senior leadership, and strengthen business continuity for critical systems.

Set performance expectations and service standards; recruit, develop, and retain staff and build depth through cross-training and succession planning. Other duties as assigned in support of the mission and priorities of the McCombs School of Business.

Experience with technology budgeting, vendor management, contracting, procurement, and major technology investments.
Knowledge of cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity, data management, and IT governance.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior executives, communicate complex technology issues to nontechnical audiences, and make sound recommendations involving cost, risk, and priorities.
Demonstrated success working with varied stakeholders and leading through influence in a complex organization.
Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate

Experience serving as a CIO, CTO, senior technology executive, or in a comparable enterprise technology leadership role.
Experience leading technology in higher education, government, another public institution, or a similarly complex, mission-driven organization, particularly within Texas.
Experience working within a federated or decentralized technology environment.
Experience with application development, system integration, data and analytics, enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, cybersecurity, and project portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience modernizing legacy applications or reducing significant technical debt.
